communityVoices.quote: The band sounds as if they were downright arrogant, like they knew they were at the very top of their game.
If anyone ever tries to explain why we love this band so much start them with this
Slipknot thru Franklins Tower was mastered at the Winterland.
it just meanders a bit to much for my tastes but thats probably why some folks love it so much
Phil Lesh came up to me in the kitchen of the main office and told me that everyone was happy to have me there and gave me his home phone number

whyThisShow: This is a broadly canonical June '77 Winterland night, officially released as part of Winterland June 1977: The Complete Recordings — the band's organization put their name on it. One longtime fan who had been seeing the Dead since 1967 called it "probably the best Grateful Dead show I've ever been too, or at least in the top 3-5". The Help>Slip>Franklin's is the centerpiece the community keeps returning to, with one reviewer arguing "Slipknot thru Franklins Tower was mastered at the Winterland", while another finds it meanders and scores it a four against the show's five. That specific disagreement over the suite has been a running community conversation, with the 5/9/77 Buffalo version frequently named as the comparison point.
listenFor: The Help>Slip>Franklin's runs roughly ten minutes longer than the 5/9/77 version, and one listener pinpoints "the last 4 minutes or so which wrap up the song in a nice breezy relaxed fashion" as the highlight. Jerry's vocals throughout the night drew particular attention — one reviewer wrote "I don't think I have ever heard Jerry sing better" and described being "mesmerized by how PERFECT his voice sounded". The second set's Estimated Prophet and the run through Eyes of the World were singled out, with one fan noting "Estimated, esp. Jerry's guitar lines" as among their favorite versions. The Mississippi Half-Step opener is flagged as a good omen by one reviewer, who notes "half step opener usually a good sign" before the second set "just explode[s] with musical energy".
context: June 9, 1977 is the third night of a three-night Winterland run, deep in the peak '77 tour. The show is available here as a soundboard recording (identifier: gd77-06-09.sbd.murphy.5597.sbefail.shnf). It was officially released as part of Winterland June 1977: The Complete Recordings. One fan noted the circulating copies had "pitch problems and a cut here and there" before the official release, which is part of why the official vault version was welcomed.
funFact: One reviewer got their original tape of this show from a co-worker at BASS tickets in Oakland named David Gans, and later received vault cassette copies directly from Phil Lesh after asking him in the office kitchen — copies that were subsequently used "in the beginning of the Grateful Dead Hour".
headline: Three nights at Winterland, and this one's the vault copy.
